title: Stripe checkout completion is not idempotent
summary: Every checkout.session.completed webhook reaches order creation without a prior duplicate check or a database uniqueness constraint on the Stripe session id.
why_it_matters: A replayed or retried completion can create another order, resend confirmation mail, and repeat cart deletion for the same paid checkout.

evidence.note: Dispatches completion handling for each checkout.session.completed payload.
Creates an order without checking for an existing Stripe session id.
Defines stripe_checkout_session_id without a unique constraint.
Deletes the cart and sends confirmation after creating the order.

recommendation: Make completion idempotent using a unique database constraint and an atomic existing-order check before creating the order; ensure duplicate deliveries do not resend mail or repeat cart cleanup.
verification_notes: Static trace was cross-checked against the orders migration and live SQLite schema. No runtime duplicate event was generated.

title: Commerce foreign-key columns have no database constraints
summary: The commerce schema stores relationships as unsigned integer columns without foreign keys, so orphaned carts, cart items, variants, orders, and order items are not prevented by the database.
why_it_matters: Application-level Eloquent relationships can return missing related records or preserve invalid references after deletes, undermining order and cart data integrity.

evidence.note: product_id is an integer without a foreign-key declaration.
user_id is an integer without a foreign-key declaration.
cart_id and product_variant_id have no foreign keys.
user_id has no foreign key.
order_id and product_variant_id have no foreign keys.

evidence.reference: live SQLite schema: cart_items and carts
evidence.note: foreign_keys is [] and sqlite_master has no REFERENCES clauses for the commerce tables.

recommendation: Add forward-only constraints for each relationship with explicitly chosen delete behavior, then validate existing data before applying them.
verification_notes: Migration source and the configured SQLite schema were both inspected; no foreign keys were reported.

title: Checkout formats cart variants without eager loading
summary: Checkout explicitly eager-loads product but accesses each cart item's variant inside the item map without eager loading the variant relation.
why_it_matters: Checkout requests with multiple cart items can issue one additional variant query per item, increasing database round trips on a payment-start path.

evidence.note: Loads product only.
Maps every cart item and reads variant fields at lines 45-46.
variant() is a BelongsTo relation.
Passes the cart item collection into the formatter.

recommendation: Eager-load variant together with product before mapping the cart items, and add a query-count regression test for a multi-item cart.
verification_notes: The relationship definition and formatter access were traced statically; no production query trace was available.

title: Order history loads every order item in one request
summary: The authenticated orders page retrieves the user's complete order-item history with get() and has no pagination or limit.
why_it_matters: The response and memory cost grow with a user's entire purchase history rather than with a bounded page size.

evidence.note: Exposes orders behind auth middleware.
Loads the complete order-item history with latest()->get().
No orders page test establishes a bounded result requirement.

recommendation: Use pagination or another explicit bound for order history and verify the intended display behavior with a feature test.
verification_notes: The route and query were inspected directly; dataset size in production was not available.

title: Payment completion and order persistence lack integration coverage
summary: The test inventory covers checkout-session creation but has no test for Stripe webhook dispatch, checkout completion, order creation, cart cleanup, or confirmation mail.
why_it_matters: The highest-value state transition in the shop is unprotected by an executable test, including the replay-sensitive behavior identified above.

evidence.note: Tests checkout-session creation only and mocks Checkout.
Contains webhook dispatch.
Contains webhook-to-order persistence.
No StripeEventListener or StripeCheckoutSessionCompleted test is present.

recommendation: Add integration coverage for a valid completion, duplicate completion, missing/invalid metadata, persisted order items, cart cleanup, and confirmation-mail behavior.
verification_notes: Test inventory and source search were cross-checked. Full execution was blocked by the environment's inability to bind a local browser-test port.

title: Admin-panel authorization boundary is not tested
summary: The application gates Filament access by configured admin email, but the test suite does not verify that the configured administrator is accepted and another authenticated user is rejected.
why_it_matters: A regression in the panel-access predicate could expose product and customer-order administration or lock out the only intended administrator without a failing test.

evidence.note: User implements FilamentUser.
Panel access compares the user's email with config('app.admin_email').
Registers the admin panel and authentication middleware.
Tests table behavior without actingAs(), canAccessPanel(), or denied-user assertions.
The authorization collector reports no policy classes.

recommendation: Add authenticated allowed/denied panel-access tests and resource-level tests for the destructive product/order actions.
verification_notes: The access predicate, panel middleware, authorization inventory, and Filament tests were inspected. No behavior was changed or inferred beyond the missing assertions.
